title: Email Triage Agent
what: An n8n workflow that watches your Gmail inbox and, for every new email, does the tedious triage work: classifies it with AI by category and urgency, drafts a reply, and notifies you on Telegram with the summary. The draft stays in your Gmail drafts folder waiting for your review: nothing goes out to the sender without you reading it, adjusting it, and hitting send. It's the inbox pipeline with a built-in human brake.
forWho: For whoever handles a shared inbox (info@, support@, orders@) and loses the first hour of the day reading and deciding. It pays off from 15-20 emails a day; below that, manual triage is still faster than maintaining the workflow.
capabilities: Detects new emails in Gmail every minute without you having the inbox open
Classifies each email by category (inquiry, order, incident, invoice, spam...) and urgency with claude-haiku-4-5
Drafts a reply in your tone and leaves it in Gmail Drafts, addressed to the sender
Notifies you on Telegram with sender, subject, category, urgency, and a two-line summary
If the AI returns something odd, flags the email as "needs review" instead of breaking
limits: Sends no email: it creates drafts. The send button is yours and must stay yours
Doesn't delete, archive, or label emails: it doesn't touch your inbox beyond creating the draft
Doesn't handle long threads or complex attachments well: it classifies based on the message text; tough cases need a human
Doesn't decide on complaints or legal matters: its draft in those cases is just an acknowledgment for you to handle

parameters.content:
## Email triage with a human brake
Gmail Trigger → prepare → Claude classifies and drafts → Gmail draft + Telegram alert.

Before activating: 1) Gmail credential (OAuth2), 2) httpHeaderAuth credential with your Anthropic key (x-api-key header), 3) Telegram bot credential and your chat_id.

This workflow NEVER sends emails: it only creates drafts.

files.name: ai-node-prompt.md
files.content:
# The classifier's prompt ("Prepare AI request" node)

The prompt lives inside the code node, in the `system` constant. This is the base version; adapt it to your business by editing that node.

```
You are the triage assistant for a professional inbox, writing in English.
Return ONLY valid JSON with these keys:
- category: inquiry | order | incident | invoice | sales | spam | needs_review
- urgency: high | medium | low
- summary: maximum 2 sentences
- reply: a friendly, brief draft reply in English, ready to review;
  if the email is a complaint or a legal matter, the reply is just an acknowledgment of receipt.
No text outside the JSON.
```

## How to adapt it

- **Your categories**: change the list to match your business (quotes, appointments, warranties...). Always keep "needs_review" as a safety net.
- **Your tone**: add a line like "sign off as the [NAME] Team" or "use formal address".
- **Your rules**: add lines like "if they ask for a price, the reply points to the public rate sheet and never promises discounts".
- Don't ask it to decide anything irreversible: it classifies and drafts, the decisions are yours.

setup.title: Import the workflow into n8n
setup.action: In n8n: Workflows → Add workflow → ⋯ menu → Import from file, and paste the JSON from this page's flow field (copy button).
setup.expect: The canvas shows 6 nodes connected in a chain plus a yellow note.
setup.stuck: If you see "could not find property", copy again: it's usually a JSON that got cut off midway.

setup.title: Connect Gmail
setup.action: Open the "Incoming email" and "Create reply draft" nodes and create a Gmail OAuth2 credential: n8n will take you to sign in with the inbox's account and accept permissions.
setup.expect: Both nodes green, with no red credential warning.
setup.stuck: On self-hosted n8n you first need to create an OAuth project in Google Cloud (n8n shows you the exact callback URL to paste there).

setup.title: Create the Anthropic credential
setup.action: Open "Classify with Claude" → Credentials → create a Header Auth with Name: x-api-key and Value: your sk-ant-... key from console.anthropic.com.
setup.expect: The node now has the credential assigned. The key lives in n8n's credentials, never inside the node.
setup.stuck: If testing returns 401, the key was copied wrong; if 400, don't touch jsonBody: it must remain exactly ={{ JSON.stringify($json.payload) }}.

setup.title: Create the Telegram bot
setup.action: On Telegram, talk to @BotFather → /newbot → copy the token into an n8n Telegram credential. Send a message to your bot and get your chat_id (e.g. with @userinfobot); paste it into the chatId field of the "Notify on Telegram" node.
setup.expect: The Telegram node with a credential and your chat_id instead of REPLACE_CHAT_ID.
setup.stuck: If the bot doesn't reply, make sure you messaged it first: bots can't start a conversation.

setup.title: Test with a real email
setup.action: Click Test workflow, send yourself an email to the monitored inbox, and wait for the execution.
setup.expect: Green execution, a new draft in Gmail addressed to the sender, and the Telegram alert with category and summary.
setup.stuck: Open the execution and look at which node stopped: every node shows its input and output, and that's always where the clue is.

setup.title: Activate it and agree on the usage rule
setup.action: Switch it to Active. Team rule from today: drafts are reviewed and sent by hand, and anything landing in "needs_review" or high urgency gets read in full.
setup.expect: New emails arrive classified and with a draft, without you having to open n8n.

test.name: Normal test
test.input: Send to the inbox: "Hi, what are your hours on Saturday? Thanks."
test.expect: Category inquiry, low urgency, draft in the agreed tone in Drafts, and Telegram alert. No email sent.

test.name: Real urgency
test.input: Send: "URGENT: the order website has been down all morning and we have customers waiting."
test.expect: Category incident, high urgency, and the Telegram summary reflects it.

test.name: Complaint
test.input: Send a complaint email asking for a refund.
test.expect: The draft is just an acknowledgment of receipt, with no promise of a refund: the decision stays with the human.

test.name: Broken AI response
test.input: Temporarily edit the prep node's prompt to ask for "reply in verse" and run it with a test email.
test.expect: The workflow doesn't break: the email comes out as category "needs_review" with a generic draft. Undo the change afterward.

credentials.name: Gmail (OAuth2)
credentials.where: Inside n8n, when opening the Gmail nodes → Create new credential
credentials.how: Sign in with the inbox account and accept the permissions. On self-hosted n8n, first create the OAuth project at console.cloud.google.com with the callback URL n8n gives you.

credentials.name: Anthropic API
credentials.how: Create the key and store it in an n8n Header Auth credential (Name: x-api-key). Never paste it into a node.
credentials.cost: pay per token; classifying an email with claude-haiku-4-5 costs a fraction of a cent

credentials.name: Telegram bot
credentials.how: Copy the token into an n8n Telegram credential and your chat_id into the alert node.

risks: Sending by mistake instead of saving a draft if someone "improves" the workflow. Mitigation: the Gmail node uses the draft resource; any change to direct sending must go through team agreement, not an afternoon of inspiration.
Email content travels to the Anthropic API. Mitigation: don't use this workflow on inboxes that receive sensitive data (health, legal) without reviewing your API account's data policy.

Blind trust in the category: a mislabeled "spam" buries an important email. Mitigation: the workflow doesn't archive or delete anything; check the full inbox once a day for the first two weeks and adjust the prompt based on the misses.
Email loop if the inbox replies to itself. Mitigation: don't activate the workflow on the same account you use to mass-send drafts to third parties; the manual draft step already breaks the loop.

examples.name: Adjust categories
examples.prompt: Edit the "Prepare AI request" node and replace the list with: enrollment | scholarship | certificate | complaint | other. Keep "needs_review" and test again with three real emails.

examples.name: Only alert on the urgent ones
examples.prompt: Add an IF node between "Parse response" and the Telegram alert with the condition urgency = high, and connect the false branch directly to the draft.
